title: Paired-face horn filtration for the fixed-source twisted-arrow simplex
statement:
Use standard simplices and horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $n\geq1$ and $V_n=\{0,1,\ldots,2n+1\}$ with its usual order. For a nonempty $S\subseteq V_n$, let $\Delta^S$ be the face of $\Delta^{2n+1}$ spanned by $S$. Say that $S$ is basic if $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n\}$ or $S\cap\{i,2n+1-i\}=\varnothing$ for some $0\leq i\leq n$. Let $K_0$ be the union of all basic faces. For a nonbasic $S$, define
$$\operatorname{pr}(S)=\max\{i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}:2n+1-i\in S\};$$
this maximum exists because $S$ is not contained in $\{0,\ldots,n\}$. Call $S$ prioritized if $\operatorname{pr}(S)\in S$. Enumerate all prioritized nonbasic subsets as $S_1,\ldots,S_m$, in nondecreasing priority and, among those of equal priority, in nondecreasing cardinality; ties may be ordered arbitrarily. Put $K_q=K_0\cup\bigcup_{a=1}^q\Delta^{S_a}$. For every $1\leq q\leq m$, write $S_q=\{j_0<\cdots<j_d\}$ and $\operatorname{pr}(S_q)=j_k$. Under the vertex-order identification $\Delta^{S_q}\cong\Delta^d$, one has
$$\Delta^{S_q}\cap K_{q-1}=\Lambda_k^d.$$
Moreover, $S_m=V_n$ and $K_m=\Delta^{2n+1}$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 8.1.2.1, basic subsets, priority ordering, and the assertion that each attaching intersection is the horn $\Lambda^d_k$.

proof.text: The collection of nonempty subsets of the finite ordered set $V_n$ is finite, so the basic/nonbasic and prioritized/nonprioritized classifications and the stated priority-then-cardinality ordering are well-defined. For each prioritized $S_q$, put $i=\operatorname{pr}(S_q)$ and write $S_q=\{j_0<\cdots<j_d\}$ with $i=j_k$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 8.1.2.1, setup of basic subsets and the ordered list (lines 31--55).

proof.text: Fix $q$ and set $S'=S_q\setminus\{i\}$. It is not basic: containment in the first block would make $S_q$ basic, and omission of some paired set $\{r,2n+1-r\}$ would also make $S_q$ basic because $2n+1-i\in S_q$. Moreover $\operatorname{pr}(S')=i$, while $i\notin S'$, so $S'$ is not prioritized. If its face were in $K_{q-1}$, it would lie in an earlier prioritized face $S_{q'}$ (it is not basic). Since $2n+1-i\in S_{q'}$, the priority of $S_{q'}$ is at least $i$; the ordering and $q'<q$ force priority $i$ and $|S_{q'}|\le |S_q|$. Prioritization then puts $i$ in $S_{q'}$, so $S_q=S'\cup\{i\}\subseteq S_{q'}$ and the cardinality inequality forces equality, contradicting $q'<q$. Thus the face omitting $i$ is not in $K_{q-1}$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 8.1.2.1, proof of the missing priority face (lines 65--73).

proof.text: If $j\in S_q$ with $j\ne i$, let $T=S_q\setminus\{j\}$. If $T$ is basic, its face is already in $K_0$. Otherwise let $i'=\operatorname{pr}(T)$; deletion cannot increase the maximum, so $i'\le i$. If $i'<i$, adjoining $i'$ to $T$ gives a prioritized nonbasic subset of smaller priority and hence one of the earlier $S_{q'}$; if $i'=i$, then $i\in T$, so $T$ itself is prioritized of priority $i$ and has cardinality $|S_q|-1$, hence also occurs earlier among the equal-priority subsets. In both cases the face of $T$ lies in $K_{q-1}$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 8.1.2.1, proof of the other deleted faces (lines 74--75).

proof.text: Every proper face of the face spanned by $S_q$ is contained in a codimension-one face obtained by deleting a vertex. By the preceding two steps, all codimension-one faces except the one deleting $j_k=i$ lie in $K_{q-1}$, while that one does not. Therefore the intersection with $K_{q-1}$ is precisely the union of the faces other than the $k$th face. By the horn definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], this union is $\Lambda_k^d$ under the vertex-order identification.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 8.1.2.1, identification of $L=\Lambda_k^d$ (lines 54--57 and 65--75).

proof.text: The full subset $V_n$ is nonbasic, has priority $n$, contains that priority, and has the largest possible cardinality among the prioritized subsets. Hence it is the final $S_m$. Since its face is the whole $\Delta^{2n+1}$, the final union is $K_m=\Delta^{2n+1}$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 8.1.2.1, end of the ordered filtration (lines 46--53).

lean.statement: theorem horn_filtration (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (m : ℕ) (S : Fin m → Finset (Fin (2 * n + 2))) (hS : Function.Injective S) (hEnum : ∀ T : Finset (Fin (2 * n + 2)), (∃ a : Fin m, S a = T) ↔ IsPrioritized n T) (hPriority : Monotone (fun a ↦ priority n (S a))) (hCard : ∀ a b : Fin m, a ≤ b → priority n (S a) = priority n (S b) → (S a).card ≤ (S b).card) : (∀ (a : Fin m) (d : ℕ) (e : Fin (d + 1) ≃o ↥(S a)) (k : Fin (d + 1)), (e k).val.val = priority n (S a) → (stage.{u} n S a.val).preimage ((stdSimplex.isoOfRepresentableBy (stdSimplex.faceRepresentableBy (S a) d e)).hom ≫ (stdSimplex.face (S a)).ι) = horn d k) ∧ (∃ last : Fin m, last.val + 1 = m ∧ S last = Finset.univ) ∧ stage.{u} n S m = ⊤
lean.note: The auxiliary definitions spell out notions defined inline by this same node. The intersection is the inverse image along the ordered face isomorphism, as in Kerodon 03JW. Fin m indexes the paper's S_1,...,S_m by a.val+1.
